claim: Preadipocytes are crucial for healthy adipose tissue expansion.
source: Preadipocytes are crucial for healthy adipose tissue expansion.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by the citation to Berry et al., 2016 in the introduction.

claim: Preadipocyte differentiation is altered in obese individuals.
source: Preadipocyte differentiation is altered in obese individuals, which has been proposed to contribute to obesity-associated metabolic disturbances.
evidence: This statement is made in the abstract and is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Down-regulation of PRPF8/PRP8 is observed in IR/T2D preadipocytes from subcutaneous fat.
source: We report that down-regulation of a key member of the major spliceosome, PRFP8/PRP8, as observed in IR/T2D preadipocytes from subcutaneous (SC) fat, prevented adipogenesis by altering both the expression and splicing patterns of adipogenic transcription factors and lipid droplet-related proteins
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR dynamic array data and protein quantification shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Down-regulation of PRPF8/PRP8 prevented adipogenesis by altering the expression and splicing patterns of adipogenic transcription factors and lipid droplet-related proteins.
source: We report that down-regulation of a key member of the major spliceosome, PRFP8/PRP8, as observed in IR/T2D preadipocytes from subcutaneous (SC) fat, prevented adipogenesis by altering both the expression and splicing patterns of adipogenic transcription factors and lipid droplet-related proteins
evidence: This claim is supported by the silencing experiments in SGBS cells and primary preadipocytes shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Adipocyte differentiation was restored upon recovery of PRPF8/PRP8 normal levels.
source: while adipocyte differentiation was restored upon recovery of PRFP8/PRP8 normal levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by the rescue experiments shown in Figures 3I and 4.

claim: Adipocyte differentiation was compromised under conditions of ERAD hyperactivation, as occurs in SC and OM preadipocytes in IR/T2D obesity.
source: Adipocyte differentiation was also compromised under conditions of endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-associated protein degradation (ERAD) hyperactivation, as occurs in SC and omental (OM) preadipocytes in IR/T2D obesity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the ERAD gene expression data in Figure 6 and the HGHI treatment experiments in Figure 7.

claim: Preadipocyte differentiation into adipocytes enables adipocyte turnover and adipose tissue growth.
source: Preadipocytes differentiation into adipocytes, i.e. adipogenesis, enables adipocyte turnover and adipose tissue growth and ensures adipose tissue plasticity to accommodate surplus energy (Arner et al., 2010; Sarjeant and Stephens, 2019; Spalding et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The inability for recruiting new adipose cells together with the functional impairment of hypertrophied adipocytes in obesity contribute to lipid spill over from the adipose tissue.
source: It has been proposed that the inability for recruiting new adipose cells together with the functional impairment of hypertrophied adipocytes that occur in obesity contribute to lipid spill over from the adipose tissue (Lessard and Tchernof, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Ectopic fat deposition and lipotoxicity in non-adipose organs have been associated with the development of insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes.
source: Ectopic fat deposition and lipotoxicity in non-adipose organs have been associated with the development of insulin resistance (IR) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) (Engin and Engin, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Alternative splicing is crucial for genome reprogramming during cell differentiation.
source: An increasing body of evidence shows that mRNA processing and, in particular, alternative splicing, is crucial for genome reprogramming during cell differentiation (Fiszbein and Kornblihtt, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: PPARγ protein variants with opposing effects on preadipocyte differentiation support a role for alternative splicing in adipogenesis.
source: In this line, the recent identification of PPARγ protein variants with opposing effects on preadipocyte differentiation, supports a role for alternative splicing in adipogenesis (Aprile et al., 2020; Aprile et al., 2018; Aprile et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The unfolded protein response is perturbed in the obese adipose tissue and has been proposed to contribute to the pathology of obesity.
source: In fact, the unfolded protein response (UPR) is perturbed in the obese adipose tissue and has been proposed to contribute to the pathology of obesity (Yilmaz, 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Genetic ablation of the core ERAD protein, SEL1L, in mouse adipocytes causes lipodystrophy and postprandial hyperlipidaemia.
source: Importantly, genetic ablation of the core ERAD protein, SEL1L, in mouse adipocytes causes lipodystrophy and postprandial hyperlipidaemia (Sha et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Down-regulation of multiple components of the splicing machinery was observed in SC preadipocytes from obese individuals with insulin resistance or T2D, as compared to NG obesity.
source: Down-regulation of multiple components of the splicing machinery was observed in SC preadipocytes from obese individuals with insulin resistance (IR) or T2D, as compared to NG obesity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR dynamic array data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Not only the UPR but also the ERAD system are altered in human SC and OM preadipocytes from IR/T2D obese subjects.
source: In addition, our studies show that not only the UPR but also the ERAD system are altered in human SC and OM preadipocytes from IR/T2D obese subjects
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Hyperactivated ERAD, when mimicked in vitro, prevented adipogenesis.
source: and that this condition (i.e., hyperactivated ERAD), when mimicked in vitro, prevented adipogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the HGHI treatment experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: A total of 78 morbidly obese subjects (BMI >40 kg/m2) were recruited.
source: Preadipocytes from SC and OM adipose tissue were isolated from 78 morbidly obese subjects (BMI <40 kg/m2) (hereinafter referred to as obese individuals) (Table 1)
evidence: This is a description of the study cohort.

claim: IFG individuals exhibited significantly higher HOMA-IR values than NG individuals.
source: IFG individuals exhibited significantly higher HOMA-IR values than NG individuals and they will be referred to as insulin-resistant (IR) subjects (Díaz-Ruiz et al., 2015; Tam et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: No significant differences were found among groups in blood pressure, inflammation, or lipid parameters except triglycerides.
source: No significant differences were found among groups in blood pressure, inflammation, or lipid parameters except triglycerides, whose levels were enhanced in T2D vs. NG obese groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Triglyceride levels were enhanced in T2D vs. NG obese groups.
source: No significant differences were found among groups in blood pressure, inflammation, or lipid parameters except triglycerides, whose levels were enhanced in T2D vs. NG obese groups.
evidence: This claim is supported by the data in Table 1.

claim: Mature adipocytes were larger in IR/T2D than in NG obese individuals.
source: Microscopic analysis of freshly isolated mature adipocytes revealed that these cells were larger in IR/T2D than in NG obese individuals (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the microscopic analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Expression levels of the proliferation marker, KI67, and the proliferation rate were higher in SC than in OM preadipocytes.
source: Expression levels of the proliferation marker, KI67, and the proliferation rate, as assessed by cell count, were higher in SC than in OM preadipocytes, and both parameters decreased in IR/T2D (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Expression levels of KI67 and proliferation rate decreased in IR/T2D.
source: Expression levels of the proliferation marker, KI67, and the proliferation rate, as assessed by cell count, were higher in SC than in OM preadipocytes, and both parameters decreased in IR/T2D (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Preadipocyte proliferation rate negatively correlated with obesity and IR markers (BMI, glucose, insulin, and HbA1c).
source: Preadipocyte proliferation rate negatively correlated with obesity and IR markers (BMI, glucose, insulin, and HbA1c) (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the correlation analysis presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: SC and OM preadipocytes from NG obese subjects differentiated well, while those from IR/T2D obese groups differentiated poorly.
source: Microscopic observation of lipid droplets (LDs) showed that both SC and OM preadipocytes from NG obese subjects differentiated well, while those from IR/T2D obese groups differentiated poorly (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the microscopic observations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The mRNA levels of PPARG, FABP4, and ADIPOQ were lower in IR obese subjects than in their NG counterparts throughout differentiation.
source: In this line, the mRNA levels of the adipocyte markers, PPARG, FABP4, and ADIPOQ were lower in IR obese subjects than in their NG counterparts throughout differentiation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: A total of 1758 proteins were identified in both SC and OM fat from NG and T2D obese individuals, defining the human obese preadipocyte proteome.
source: This study enabled the identification of a total of 1758 proteins that were present in both SC and OM fat from NG and T2D obese individuals, thus defining the human obese preadipocyte proteome.
evidence: This claim is based on the iTRAQ proteomic analysis described in the manuscript.

claim: 55.5% of the identified proteins were related to cellular and metabolic processes according to GO Biological Process annotation.
source: According to GO Biological Process annotation, 55.5% of these proteins were related to cellular and metabolic processes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: This claim is supported by the GO analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The highest ranked down-regulated pathway in SC preadipocytes in T2D obesity was the spliceosomal cycle.
source: Among the top ten IPA canonical pathways that were overrepresented in SC preadipocytes in T2D obesity (Figure 1—source data 2), the highest ranked down-regulated pathway was the spliceosomal cycle (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the IPA canonical pathway analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The unfolded protein response was modified in SC preadipocytes from T2D obese group.
source: The unfolded protein response (UPR) was also modified in SC preadipocytes from T2D obese group (Figure 1B)
evidence: This claim is supported by the IPA canonical pathway analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Pathways related to ER stress were up-regulated in OM preadipocytes in T2D vs. NG obesity.
source: while pathways related to ER stress were up-regulated in OM preadipocytes (Figure 1C) in T2D vs. NG obesity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the IPA canonical pathway analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: SC preadipocytes from IR/T2D obese individuals exhibited lower expression levels of splicing-related genes than NG obese subjects.
source: SC preadipocytes from IR/T2D obese individuals exhibited lower expression levels of splicing-related genes than NG obese subjects, including components of major spliceosome (PRPF8, RNU5, SF3B1 tv1, TCERG1, and U2AF1), and splicing factors (CELF1, MAGOH, RBM3, RBM45, SFPQ, and SNW1) (Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR dynamic array data shown in Figure 2A and B, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Only the minor spliceosome component, RNU12, was up-regulated in T2D vs. NG SC preadipocytes.
source: Notably, only the minor spliceosome component, RNU12, was up-regulated in T2D vs. NG SC preadipocytes (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR dynamic array data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: No differences in OM preadipocytes were observed among the three groups of obese individuals.
source: No differences in OM preadipocytes were observed among the three groups of obese individuals (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR dynamic array data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Significantly higher expression levels of main components of the major spliceosome (PRPF8 and SF3B1 tv1) were observed in SC preadipocytes from NG obese vs. lean individuals.
source: These results revealed significantly higher expression levels of main components of the major spliceosome (PRPF8 and SF3B1 tv1) in SC preadipocytes from NG obese vs. lean individuals (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: A significant decrease in the expression levels of all the genes tested, except RNU12, was observed in T2D vs. NG individuals with simple obesity.
source: Notably, and similar to that observed for morbidly obese individuals from cohort 1 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplements 1 and 2), a significant decrease in the expression levels of all the genes tested, except RNU12, was observed in T2D vs. NG individuals with simple obesity (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: mRNA and protein levels of PRPF8/PRP8 were reduced by 51% and 56%, respectively, in IR SC preadipocytes as compared to NG levels.
source: Specifically, mRNA and protein levels of this key component of the major spliceosome were reduced by 51% and 56%, respectively, in IR SC preadipocytes, and by 49% and 82% in T2D SC preadipocytes as compared to NG levels (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: mRNA and protein levels of PRPF8/PRP8 were reduced by 49% and 82%, respectively, in T2D SC preadipocytes as compared to NG levels.
source: Specifically, mRNA and protein levels of this key component of the major spliceosome were reduced by 51% and 56%, respectively, in IR SC preadipocytes, and by 49% and 82% in T2D SC preadipocytes as compared to NG levels (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: PRPF8 expression levels remained low throughout adipogenesis in IR preadipocytes.
source: Differentiation studies revealed that while PRPF8 expression levels remained low throughout adipogenesis in IR preadipocytes, PRPF8 levels peaked at day 3 (D3) of differentiation and thereafter remained above D0 levels in NG preadipocytes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: PRPF8 levels peaked at day 3 of differentiation and thereafter remained above D0 levels in NG preadipocytes.
source: Differentiation studies revealed that while PRPF8 expression levels remained low throughout adipogenesis in IR preadipocytes, PRPF8 levels peaked at day 3 (D3) of differentiation and thereafter remained above D0 levels in NG preadipocytes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: siRNA treatment of SGBS preadipocytes decreased by 67% and 65% PRPF8 mRNA and protein levels, respectively, at day 3 post-transfection.
source: siRNA treatment of SGBS preadipocytes (D4) decreased by 67% and 65% PRPF8 mRNA and protein levels, respectively, at day 3 post-transfection (D7), without changing cell viability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: PRPF8-silenced preadipocytes accumulated more but smaller LDs than control cells.
source: Morphometric evaluation of Oil-Red O staining in confocal micrographs revealed that PRPF8-silenced preadipocytes accumulated more but smaller LDs than control cells, which resulted in an increase in the total lipid content in cells exposed to PRPF8 siRNA (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PRPF8-silenced cells resulted in an increase in the total lipid content.
source: Morphometric evaluation of Oil-Red O staining in confocal micrographs revealed that PRPF8-silenced preadipocytes accumulated more but smaller LDs than control cells, which resulted in an increase in the total lipid content in cells exposed to PRPF8 siRNA (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PPARG and SREBF1 are PRP8 target genes according to in silico analysis of CLIP_Seq data.
source: In silico analysis of CLIP_Seq data using ENCORI (The Encyclopedia of RNA Interactomes) (Li et al., 2014) revealed both adipogenic (PPARG and SREBF1) and LD biogenesis and growth markers (BSCL2, CIDEB, and CIDEC) as PRP8 target genes (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is based on in silico analysis of CLIP_Seq data.

claim: BSCL2, CIDEB, and CIDEC are PRP8 target genes according to in silico analysis of CLIP_Seq data.
source: In silico analysis of CLIP_Seq data using ENCORI (The Encyclopedia of RNA Interactomes) (Li et al., 2014) revealed both adipogenic (PPARG and SREBF1) and LD biogenesis and growth markers (BSCL2, CIDEB, and CIDEC) as PRP8 target genes (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is based on in silico analysis of CLIP_Seq data.

claim: Enrichment analysis of PRP8-RNA interactions revealed pathways such as insulin signalling, adipokine signalling, and fatty acid metabolism to be significantly overrepresented.
source: Enrichment analysis of PRP8-RNA interactions revealed pathways such as insulin signalling, adipokine signalling, and fatty acid metabolism to be significantly overrepresented (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is based on enrichment analysis of PRP8-RNA interactions.

claim: Expression of total PPARG and SREBF1 transcript contents and the abundances of some of their isoforms were altered in PRPF8-silenced cells.
source: In accordance with the in silico data, expression of total PPARG and SREBF1 transcript contents and the abundances of some of their isoforms were altered in PRPF8-silenced cells (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: mRNA and protein levels of the fat-specific PPARG isoform, PPARG-2, were up-regulated upon PRPF8 silencing.
source: In particular, mRNA and protein levels of the fat-specific PPARG isoform, PPARG-2, were up-regulated upon PRPF8 silencing (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Decreased levels and/or altered splicing patterns of BSCL2, CIDEB, and CIDEC were observed in PRPF8-silenced cells.
source: Decreased levels and/or altered splicing patterns of BSCL2, CIDEB, and CIDEC, were also observed in silenced cells (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: PRPF8 silencing activated stress responses in SGBS adipocytes, as indicated by the increased protein levels of CHOP, PSMB8, and CASP3/Pro-CASP3 ratio.
source: PRPF8 silencing also activated stress responses in SGBS adipocytes, as indicated by the increased protein levels of the ER stress marker, CHOP, the immunoproteasome compkeonent, PSMB8, and CASP3/Pro-CASP3 ratio (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: PRPF8-silenced cells did not respond to an insulin challenge.
source: Contrarily to control cells, PRPF8-silenced cells did not respond to an insulin challenge (Figure 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Recovery of PRP8 protein levels by co-transfection of PRPF8-silenced SGBS cells with an expression vector coding for this protein reverted the effects induced by PRPF8 silencing on adipocyte and LD markers.
source: Notably, recovery of PRP8 protein levels by co-transfection of PRPF8-silenced SGBS cells with an expression vector coding for this protein (PRPF8-pcDNA3.1) reverted the effects induced by PRPF8 silencing on adipocyte and LD markers, both at D7 (data not shown) and D10 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the rescue experiments shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Silencing-induced changes in both LD number and size were reverted in rescue experiments by PRPF8 re-expression.
source: Silencing-induced changes in both LD number and size were also reverted in rescue experiments by PRPF8 re-expression (Figure 3I).
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 3I.

claim: Exposure to pladienolide-B impaired lipid accumulation in SGBS cells.
source: Exposure to pladienolide-B impaired lipid accumulation in SGBS cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: SFPQ down-regulation by siRNA treatment of SGBS cells caused significant changes in the expression of only a few genes.
source: On the other hand, SFPQ down-regulation by siRNA treatment of SGBS cells caused significant changes in the expression of only a few genes, i.e., up-regulation of total SREBF1 and SREBF1-1 and down-regulation of PPARG-4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D-G.

claim: SFPQ-silenced SGBS cells exhibited reduced lipid content, mostly due to the increase in the number of LDs.
source: Nevertheless, silenced SGBS cells exhibited reduced lipid content, mostly due to the increase in the number of LDs (2.4-fold), while LD size decreased as compared with control cells (2.7-fold) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: SC preadipocytes from NG obese individuals exhibited lower lipid content and changes in LD size and number when silenced for PRPF8.
source: As shown in Figure 4B, SC preadipocytes from NG obese individuals exhibited lower lipid content and changes in LD size and number when silenced for PRPF8.
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: PRPF8 down-regulation caused numerical decreases in the expression levels of both total PPARG and SREBF1 and their isoforms as compared to mock-transfected SC preadipocytes from NG obese subjects.
source: In addition, PRPF8 down-regulation caused numerical decreases, that in most cases reached statistical significance, in the expression levels of both total PPARG and SREBF1 and their isoforms as compared to mock-transfected SC preadipocytes from NG obese subjects (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4C–D.

claim: Rescue experiments by transfection of silenced NG obese preadipocytes with the PRPF8-pcDNA3.1 expression vector showed restored expression of most of the genes tested.
source: Notably, rescue experiments by transfection of silenced NG obese preadipocytes with the PRPF8-pcDNA3.1 expression vector showed restored expression of most of the genes tested, which was accompanied by a recovery of LD content (Figure 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR and confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 4.

claim: PRPF8 expression recovery upon PRPF8-pcDNA3.1 transfection increased the expression of several PPARG isoforms to control levels, especially in IR preadipocytes.
source: PRPF8 expression recovery upon PRPF8-pcDNA3.1 transfection increased the expression of several PPARG isoforms (PPARG-2, PPARG-3, PPARG-4, and γORF4) to control levels (i.e. SC preadipocytes in NG obesity), especially in IR preadipocytes (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: PRPF8-pcDNA3.1 expression increased total lipid content in SC preadipocytes from obese subjects with IR/T2D by increasing LD size, while decreasing LD number.
source: In line with these findings, confocal microscopy studies showed that PRPF8-pcDNA3.1 expression increased total lipid content in SC preadipocytes from obese subjects with IR/T2D by increasing LD size, while decreasing LD number (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the confocal microscopy and morphometric analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: SC and OM preadipocytes from T2D obese individuals exhibited enhanced levels of BiP.
source: To be more specific, SC and OM preadipocytes from T2D obese individuals exhibited enhanced levels of the ER stress-inducible gene, BiP (Figure 5A and Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: IR/T2D modified the protein content of p90 and p50, and cleaved/full-length ATF6 ratio in OM preadipocytes.
source: IR/T2D modified the protein content of p90 and p50, and cleaved/full-length ATF6 ratio in OM preadipocytes, and decreased this ratio in SC preadipocytes in IR vs. NG (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: pPERK and pPERK/PERK ratio were up-regulated in SC and OM preadipocytes in relation to IR and/or T2D.
source: In addition, pPERK and pPERK/PERK ratio were up-regulated in SC and OM preadipocytes in relation to IR and/or T2D (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: peIF2α and peIF2α/eIF2α ratio as well as the eIF2α-target, CHOP, were significantly reduced in OM preadipocytes in relation to IR/T2D.
source: However, peIF2α and peIF2α/eIF2α ratio as well as the eIF2α-target, CHOP, were significantly reduced in OM preadipocytes in relation to IR/T2D (Figure 5C and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 5C and E.

claim: Enhanced IRE1α levels and decreased pIRE1α/IRE1α ratio were observed in IR vs. NG OM preadipocytes.
source: We observed enhanced IRE1α levels and decreased pIRE1α/IRE1α ratio in IR vs. NG OM preadipocytes (Figure 5F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: IR OM preadipocytes and IR/T2D SC preadipocytes exhibited higher levels of the spliced form of XBP1 than NG preadipocytes.
source: IR OM preadipocytes and IR/T2D SC preadipocytes also exhibited higher levels of the spliced form of XBP1 than NG preadipocytes (Figure 5G).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The ER chaperones, GRP94 and PDI, were more abundant in T2D preadipocytes than in NG preadipocytes from both SC and OM fat.
source: Finally, the ER chaperones, GRP94 and PDI, were more abundant in T2D preadipocytes than in NG preadipocytes from both SC and OM fat (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by the western blot data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: A marked up-regulation of proteins involved in all the steps comprising ERAD was observed in IR/T2D vs. NG obesity.
source: Given our results on the UPR, we next explored the ERAD in human preadipocytes and observed a marked up-regulation of proteins involved in all the steps comprising this process, including protein recognition (BIP; Figure 6A), retrotranslocation through the ER membrane (DERL1, SEC61A1, STT3A, and STT3B; Figure 6B), ubiquitination (HRD1 and RNF185; Figure 6C), and targeting of misfolded proteins to the proteasome (RAD23A and UBQLN1; Figure 6D) in IR/T2D vs. NG obesity.
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6A-D.

claim: SC and OM preadipocytes split into two clusters (NG and IR/T2D) when ERAD data was represented in a two-way hierarchical clustering heatmap.
source: These changes occurred in both SC and OM preadipocytes, which split into two clusters (NG and IR/T2D) when ERAD data was represented in a two-way hierarchical clustering heatmap (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the hierarchical clustering analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Higher overall transcript contents of ERAD genes in IR preadipocytes than in NG preadipocytes were observed during adipocyte differentiation.
source: In this line, when the ERAD process was explored during adipocyte differentiation, higher overall transcript contents of ERAD genes in IR preadipocytes than in NG preadipocytes (measured as AUC) were observed (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exposure to HGHI increased the expression of BiP and nearly all the other ERAD components tested in SGBS cells.
source: Exposure to HGHI increased the expression of BiP and nearly all the other ERAD components tested (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Hyperglycaemic/hyperinsulinemic conditions decreased the activity of the 26 S proteasome while increasing the amount of ubiquitinated proteins in SGBS preadipocytes.
source: These studies showed that hyperglycaemic/hyperinsulinemic conditions decreased the activity of the 26 S proteasome while increasing the amount of ubiquitinated proteins in SGBS preadipocytes (Figure 7—figure supplement 2C and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by the proteasome activity assay and western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2C and H.

claim: Exposure of SGBS preadipocytes to TUDCA prior to HGHI treatment prevented HGHI-induced up-regulation of ERAD genes and accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins.
source: We thus tested whether exposure of SGBS preadipocytes to TUDCA prior to HGHI treatment could prevent HGHI-induced up-regulation of ERAD genes and accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins in these cells, which was proven to be the case (Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D and E.

claim: TUDCA reverted HGHI inhibitory effects on PPARγ and FABP4 expression levels.
source: TUDCA also reverted HGHI inhibitory effects on PPARγ and FABP4 expression levels (Figure 7—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2F.

claim: Exposure of OM preadipocytes from NG obese subjects to HGHI increased the expression levels of genes involved in all ERAD steps.
source: Figure 7 shows that, as for SGBS preadipocytes, exposure of OM preadipocytes from NG obese subjects to HGHI increased the expression levels of genes involved in all ERAD steps (recognition, retrotranslocation ubiquitination, and targeting to the proteasome) in these cells (Figure 7A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7A–D.

claim: TUDCA reduced HGHI-induced gene expression increases to control levels in OM preadipocytes from NG obese individuals.
source: On the other hand, TUDCA, which did not alter essentially the expression of ERAD genes when administered alone, reduced HGHI-induced gene expression increases to control levels (i.e. OM preadipocytes from NG obese individuals exposed to medium alone) (Figure 7A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by the RT-PCR data shown in Figure 7A–D.

claim: HGHI increased the accumulation of ubiquitinated proteins in OM preadipocytes from NG obese individuals.
